taxYear.description: The tax year in which the calculation was performed.

requestedBy.description: The requester of the calculation. Currently "customer" will be returned even in the case of an agent submission.

requestedTimestamp.description: The timestamp of when the calculation was requested in ISO 8601 UTC format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ.

calculationReason.description:
The reason why the calculation was triggered. 

Possible values are: 

* **customer-request** - The calculation was triggered by the customer via software.

* **class2-nic-event** - The calculation was triggered internally by HMRC once the actual Class 2 NIC amount became available. This event is only applicable for an in-year "final-declaration" calculation type.

* **new-annual-adjustment-event** - The calculation was triggered internally by HMRC on receipt of a request for a new adjustable summary calculation by the customer. This event is not currently supported.

* **updated-annual-adjustment-event** - The calculation was triggered internally by HMRC on receipt of an adjustment to an adjustable summary calculation made by the customer. This event is not currently supported.

* **unattended-calculation** - HMRC has updated the calculation for you. You can see more details in your record-keeping software.

* **enquiry-amendment** - The calculation was triggered internally by HMRC following a Revenue Amendment made as part of an enquiry.

* **auto-correction** - The calculation was triggered internally by HMRC following an automatic correction made to the customer's submission.

* **manual-correction** - The calculation was triggered internally by HMRC following a manual correction made to the customer's submission.

* **marriage-allowance** - The calculation was triggered internally by HMRC following an update to the customer's Marriage Allowance.

* **class2-national-insurance** - The calculation was triggered internally by HMRC following an update to the customer's Class 2 National Insurance Contributions (NICs).

* **devolved-residency** - The calculation was triggered internally by HMRC following an update to the customer's devolved residency information.

* **customer-rejection-of-a-correction** - The calculation was triggered internally by HMRC following a customer's rejection of a correction made to their submission.

get.summary: Retrieve a Self Assessment Tax Calculation [test only]

post.description:
This endpoint allows the developer to submit a final declaration for a tax year by agreeing to the HMRC's tax calculation. 

A National Insurance number, tax year and calculation ID must be provided.

### Test data
Scenario simulations using `Gov-Test-Scenario` headers is only available in the sandbox environment.

| Header Value (Gov-Test-Scenario)   | Scenario                                                                           |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| N/A - DEFAULT                      | Simulates success response.                                                        |
| OUTSIDE_AMENDMENT_WINDOW           | Simulates the scenario where the request cannot be completed as it is outside the amendment window. |
| FINAL_DECLARATION_IN_PROGRESS      | Simulates the scenario where there is a calculation in progress for the tax year.  |
| FINAL_DECLARATION_RECEIVED         | Simulates the scenario where a final declaration has already been received.        |
| FINAL_DECLARATION_TAX_YEAR         | Simulates the scenario where the final declaration cannot be submitted until after the end of the tax year. |
| INCOME_SOURCES_CHANGED             | Simulates the scenario where information relating to an income source has changed. |
| INCOME_SOURCES_INVALID             | Simulates the scenario where a valid income source cannot be found.                |
| NO_INCOME_SUBMISSIONS_EXIST        | Simulates the scenario where no income submissions exist.                          |
| RECENT_SUBMISSIONS_EXIST           | Simulates the scenario where more recent submissions exist.                        |
| RESIDENCY_CHANGED                  | Simulates the scenario where residency has changed.                                 |
| SUBMISSION_FAILED                  | Simulates the scenario where a submission has failed.                               |
| NOT_FOUND                          | Simulates the scenario where the supplied income source could not be found.        |

parameters.description: National Insurance number, in the format `AA999999A`
parameters.name: nino

parameters.description:
The tax year the data applies to, for example, 2021-22. 
The start year and end year must not span two tax years. 
The minimum tax year is 2017-18. No gaps are allowed, for example, 2020-22 is not valid.
parameters.name: taxYear

parameters.description:
The unique identifier of the calculation.

Must conform to the regular expression: `^[0-9]{8}|[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[1-5][0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`
parameters.name: calculationId

parameters.description:
Specifies the calculation types to be confirmed. Limited to the following possible values for TY24-25 and before: final-declaration

Limited to the following possible values for TY25-26 onwards: `final-declaration` `confirm-amendment`

info.description:
# Data availability

Data is only available for taxpayers who are registered for Self Assessment and had any employments in the given tax year.

Also, data is only available once PAYE reconciliation has completed. This is the process that determines whether the individual has paid the right amount of tax and, for PAYE-only taxpayers, results in a P800 in the event of [overpayment or underpayment.](https://www.gov.uk/tax-overpayments-and-underpayments)

Reconciliation starts on or around 6th June and runs for around one million individuals per working night. It has usually completed by the end of November. Unfortunately it is not possible to know when reconciliation will be complete for a specific individual.

If we are expecting a P11D, reconciliation will not start for that individual until we have received and processed the P11D. If we receive a P11D unexpectedly, we will re-run the reconciliation.

Data is no longer available once we have received and processed the corresponding Self Assessment return.

# Data quality

The data from this API is based on information we receive from employers and pension providers.

Note that:

- Pension providers sometimes don't tell us that income has come from a pension. In these cases, 
the API reports the income source as an employment.
- If the individual received a State Pension lump sum in the given tax year, 
this API will report it as an employment with a specific PAYE reference of `267/LS500`.

# Authorisation

The endpoint in this API is [user-restricted](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/api-documentation/docs/authorisation/user-restricted-endpoints). 
Your users must grant authority for your software to access it by signing in to their HMRC online account.

The API supports individual and agent users. Note that:
- Individual users can only access their own information.
- Agent users can only access their own clients’ data.

The following options are supported for agents:

**Option 1: Agent services account**

If the agent uses an [agent services account](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/hmrc-online-services-for-agents#agent-services-account), they can access their [existing 64-8 clients](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/how-to-get-authorised-to-act-as-a-tax-agent-on-behalf-of-your-clients#get-authorised-using-online-services-online-forms-or-paper-forms) who they have linked to their agent services account (restricted to 2 years’ history).

**Option 2: HMRC online services for agents account**

If the agent uses an [HMRC online services for agents account](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/hmrc-online-services-for-agents#hmrc-online-services-for-agents-account) which is enrolled for [Self Assessment for Agents](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/self-assessment-for-agents-online-service), they will be able to access their [existing 64-8 clients](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/how-to-get-authorised-to-act-as-a-tax-agent-on-behalf-of-your-clients#get-authorised-using-online-services-online-forms-or-paper-forms) (restricted to 2 years’ history).

Data is only available for taxpayers who are registered for Self Assessment.

The majority of data will only be available once PAYE reconciliation has been completed. Data for Self-Employment Income Support Scheme (SEISS) will be available from the beginning of the next tax year following a claim. For example, if SEISS is claimed in June 2021, the data will be available on 6 April 2022. It does not need to wait for reconciliation.

This endpoint enables you to create a new brought forward loss which can be submitted against self-employment, self-employment class 4, UK Furnished Holiday Let (FHL) property, UK other (Non-FHL) property, foreign property FHL in the European Economic Area (EEA) and foreign property for the tax year prior to joining MTD. A National Insurance number and tax year must be provided. > This endpoint supports tax years up to, and including, 2025-26. For tax years 2026–27 onwards, a new version is in development. post.description:
This endpoint enables you to change the type of claim for an existing loss claim type. A National Insurance Number, tax year and Claim ID must be provided. > This endpoint supports tax years up to, and including, 2025-26. For tax years 2026–27 onwards, a new version is in development. Note: carry-sideways-fhl type of loss claims for income sources uk-property-fhl and foreign-property-fhl-eea will not be supported from tax year 2025-26 onwards. ### Test data Scenario simulation using Gov-Test-Scenario headers is only available in the sandbox environment. | Header Value (Gov-Test-Scenario) | Scenario | | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | N/A - DEFAULT | Simulates success response. | | FP_FORWARD | Simulates a Foreign Property carried forward scenario. | | FP_SIDEWAYS | Simulates a Foreign Property carried sideways scenario. | | UK_FORWARD | Simulates a UK Property (Non-FHL) carried forward scenario. | | UK_FORWARD_TO_SIDEWAYS | Simulates a UK Property (Non-FHL) carried forward to sideways scenario. | | UK_SIDEWAYS | Simulates a UK Property (Non-FHL) carried sideways scenario. | | UK_SIDEWAYS_FHL | Simulates a UK Property FHL carried sideways scenario. | | SE_FORWARD | Simulates a Self Employment carried forward scenario. | | SE_SIDEWAYS | Simulates a Self Employment carried sideways scenario. | | NO_CHANGE | Simulates the scenario where the relief type has not changed. | | TYPE_OF_CLAIM_INVALID | Simulates the scenario where a claim type is invalid for the income source. | | CSFHL_CLAIM_NOT_SUPPORTED | Simulates the scenario where carry-sideways-fhl claim submitted for income sources "FHL Property - EEA" and "UK Property FHL". | | NOT_FOUND | Simulates the scenario where no data is found. | | OUTSIDE_AMENDMENT_WINDOW | Simulates the scenario where request cannot be completed as it is outside the amendment window. | | STATEFUL | Performs a stateful update. | | DYNAMIC | The following response values will change to correspond to the values submitted in the request:
• typeOfClaim
• typeOfLoss
• lastModified |

info.description:
The following endpoints are stateful in the Sandbox: * Retrieve Losses and Claims * Create or Amend Losses and Claims * Delete Losses and Claims # Send fraud prevention data HMRC monitors transactions to help protect your customers' confidential data from criminals and fraudsters.
! Warning You are required by law to submit header data for this API. This includes all associated APIs and endpoints.
[Check the data you need to send](/guides/fraud-prevention/). You can also use the [Test API](/api-documentation/docs/api/service/txm-fph-validator-api/1.0) during initial development and as part of your quality assurance checks. # Mapping APIs to Self Assessment tax return forms Some parameters in this API map to box numbers in one or more Self Assessment tax return forms. To learn more and to download this mapping information as a CSV file, go to [income-tax-mtd-changelog/mapping](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog?tab=readme-ov-file#mapping-apis-to-self-assessment-tax-return-forms) on GitHub. # Changelog You can find the changelog in the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/#readme) on GitHub. # Support * Direct reports of bugs or errors in Production or Sandbox code, or queries about HMRC business functionality (such as how a specific field is used by HMRC or why it is needed) to the [Software Development Support Team (SDST)](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/developer/support). * Send queries or feedback related to the design of the APIs (including recommended changes) using the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/issues) GitHub page. * Is this page not working properly? carryBack.description: Object containing loss amounts to be carried back.

previousYearGeneralIncome.description: The amount of the current tax year's trading losses to carry back to be off set against general income of the previous year(s). The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

earlyYearLosses.description: The amount of the current tax year's trading losses to carry back and be set off against general income of the previous year(s). The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

terminalLosses.description: The amount of the current tax year's trading losses to be carry back and applied against profits of the three previous years, starting with the latest year first. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

carrySideways.description: Object containing loss amounts to be carried sideways to the current tax year general income.

currentYearGeneralIncome.description: The amount of the current tax year's trading losses to be off set general income of the current tax year. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

preferenceOrder.description: Object containing a preference order to be specified.

applyFirst.description:
Specifies the preference order when the current tax year's trading losses have been claimed to set against general income of a previous year and set against general income of the current tax year.

Limited to the following possible values:
* carry-sideways 
* carry-back

carryForward.description: Object containing loss amounts to be carried forward.

currentYearLosses.description: The amount of trading losses in the current tax year carried forward to offset future profits of the same trade. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

previousYearsLosses.description: The amount of trading losses from previous years carried forward to offset future profits of the same trade. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

losses.description: Object containing brought forward loss amount.

broughtForwardLosses.description: The amount of brought forward losses to be applied in the current tax year against any the current tax year profits. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

put.description:
This endpoint allows a developer to submit or amend a claim or a brought-forward-loss for a specified individual and business for a given tax year.  A National Insurance number, business ID and tax year are required.
**This endpoint can only be used after the tax year has ended.**

**Note:** It is essential that customers submit carry back losses before the final declaration when tax liability adjustments are submitted using the Create or Amend Tax Liability Adjustments endpoint in the [Individuals Tax Liability Adjustments API](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/api-documentation/docs/api/service/individuals-tax-liability-adjustments-api).

### Test data
Scenario simulation using Gov-Test-Scenario headers is only available in the sandbox environment.

| Header Value (Gov-Test-Scenario) | Scenario                                                                                         |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| N/A - DEFAULT                    | Simulates successful response.                                                                   |
| NOT_FOUND                        | Simulates the scenario where no data is found.                                                   |
| CARRY_BACK_CLAIM                 | Simulates the scenario where carry back claim type is supplied for a property income source.     |
| OUTSIDE_AMENDMENT_WINDOW         | Simulates the scenario where request cannot be completed as it is outside the amendment window.  |
| STATEFUL                         | Performs a stateful create or update.                                                            |

scopes.read:individual-tax: Access personal and employment-related tax information

info.description:
# Data availability

Data is only available for taxpayers who are registered for Self Assessment.

Also, data is only available once PAYE reconciliation has completed. This is the process that determines whether the individual has paid the right amount of tax and, for PAYE-only taxpayers, results in a P800 in the event of [overpayment or underpayment.](https://www.gov.uk/tax-overpayments-and-underpayments)

Reconciliation starts on or around 6th June and runs for around one million individuals per working night. It has usually completed by the end of November. Unfortunately it is not possible to know when reconciliation will be complete for a specific individual.

If we are expecting a P11D, reconciliation will not start for that individual until we have received and processed the P11D. If we receive a P11D unexpectedly, we will re-run the reconciliation.

Data is no longer available once we have received and processed the corresponding Self Assessment return.

# Data quality

The data from this API is based on information we receive from employers and pension providers.

Note that:

- Pension providers sometimes don't tell us that income has come from a pension. In these cases, 
the API reports the income source as an employment.
- If the individual received a State Pension lump sum in the given tax year, this API will report it as an employment 
with a specific PAYE reference of `267/LS500`.

# Authorisation

The endpoint in this API is [user-restricted](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/api-documentation/docs/authorisation/user-restricted-endpoints). 
Your users must grant authority for your software to access it by signing in to their HMRC online account.

The API supports individual and agent users. Note that:
- Individual users can only access their own information.
- Agent users can only access their own clients’ data.

The following options are supported for agents:

**Option 1: Agent services account**

If the agent uses an [agent services account](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/hmrc-online-services-for-agents#agent-services-account), they can access their [existing 64-8 clients](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/how-to-get-authorised-to-act-as-a-tax-agent-on-behalf-of-your-clients#get-authorised-using-online-services-online-forms-or-paper-forms) who they have linked to their agent services account (restricted to 2 years’ history).

**Option 2: HMRC online services for agents account**

If the agent uses an [HMRC online services for agents account](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/hmrc-online-services-for-agents#hmrc-online-services-for-agents-account) which is enrolled for [Self Assessment for Agents](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/self-assessment-for-agents-online-service), they will be able to access their [existing 64-8 clients](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/how-to-get-authorised-to-act-as-a-tax-agent-on-behalf-of-your-clients#get-authorised-using-online-services-online-forms-or-paper-forms) (restricted to 2 years’ history).

submittedOn.description: The date the disposals were submitted to the Report and pay Capital Gains Tax on UK property service. It is in the format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ.

`PRR` - Private Residence Relief where Letting Relief does not apply\

`GHO` - Gift Hold-Over Relief\

`NVC` - Negligible Value Claims\
`SIR` - Social Investment Tax Relief\

carriedInterestRttTaxPaid.description: The total amount of tax paid through the Capital Gains Tax Real Time Transactions service for all of the carried interest gains. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

attributedGains.description: The total amount of all the attributed gains where personal losses cannot be set off. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

setAgainstInYearGains.description: The total amount of trading losses set against chargeable gains for the specified tax year. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

setAgainstInYearGeneralIncome.description: The total amount of losses set against general income for the specified tax year. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

setAgainstEarlierYear.description: The total amount of losses set against general income for the tax year previous to the specified tax year. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

adjustments.description: The amount of included adjustments to reduce or increase the Capital Gains Tax payable. The value must be between -99999999999.99 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

value.supplementaryInformation: Additional information relating to the disposal of an asset and the justification for the relief code applied.

submittedOn.description: The date the disposals were submitted to the 'Report and pay Capital Gains Tax on UK property' service. It is in the format `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`.

disposals.description: An array of other Capital Gains disposals.

assetType.description: The type of asset being disposed of.

assetDescription.description: A description of the asset being disposed of. Must not be empty or contain only whitespace.

acquisitionDate.description: The date the asset was acquired in the format `YYYY-MM-DD`. For brokers' schedules where gains from several disposals are entered as one, this should be the date on which the first asset was acquired.

disposalDate.description: The date that the asset was disposed of in the format `YYYY-MM-DD`. For brokers' schedules where gains from several disposals are entered as one, this should be the date on which the last asset was disposed of.

disposalProceeds.description: The total proceeds from the disposal of the asset. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

allowableCosts.description: The total amount of allowable costs that can be deducted from the disposal proceeds. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

gain.description: The total gain from the disposal. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

loss.description: The total loss from the disposal. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

claimOrElectionCodes.description:
The claim, election or notice codes related to the disposal. Possible values are:\
`PRR` - Private Residence Relief where Letting Relief does not apply\
`LET` - Private Residence Relief where Letting Relief applies\
`GHO` - Gift Hold-Over Relief\
`ROR` - Rollover Relief\
`PRO` - Provisional Rollover Relief\
`ESH` - Employee Shares\
`NVC` - Negligible Value Claims\
`SIR` - Social Investment Tax Relief\
`OTH` - Other claims\
`BAD` - Business Asset Disposal Relief\
`INV` - Investors' Relief

gainAfterRelief.description: The total net gain after any reliefs have been applied. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

lossAfterRelief.description: The total net loss after any reliefs have been applied. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

rttTaxPaid.description: The total amount of tax paid through the Capital Gains Tax Real Time Transactions service for this disposal. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

nonStandardGains.description: One of these fields must be provided: carriedInterestGain, attributedGains or otherGains

carriedInterestGain.description: The total amount of all the carried interest gains. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

carriedInterestRttTaxPaid.description: The total amount of tax paid through the Capital Gains Tax Real Time Transactions service for all of the carried interest gains. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

attributedGains.description: The total amount of all the attributed gains where personal losses cannot be set off. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

attributedGainsRttTaxPaid.description: The total amount of tax paid through the Capital Gains Tax Real Time Transactions service for all of the attributed interest gains. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

otherGains.description: The total amount of any other asset type gains not reported elsewhere for the specified tax year. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

otherGainsRttTaxPaid.description: The total amount of tax paid through the Capital Gains Tax Real Time Transactions service on any other asset-type gains. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

losses.description: Details Capital Gains Tax losses relating to other disposals and non-standard gains. One of these fields must be provided: broughtForwardLossesUsedInCurrentYear, setAgainstInYearGains, setAgainstInYearGeneralIncome or setAgainstEarlierYear

broughtForwardLossesUsedInCurrentYear.description: The total amount of brought forward losses used for the specified tax year. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

setAgainstInYearGains.description: The total amount of trading losses set against chargeable gains for the specified tax year. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

put.description:
This endpoint enables you to submit other capital gains and disposals with the exception of residential property,
for a given National Insurance number and tax year.

### Test data
Scenario simulation using Gov-Test-Scenario headers is only available in the sandbox environment.

| Header Value (Gov-Test-Scenario) | Scenario                                                                                                 |
|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| N/A - DEFAULT                    | Simulates success response with gains.                                                                   |
| INVALID_DISPOSAL_DATE            | Simulates a scenario where disposalDate is not within the specified tax year or later than today's date. |
| INVALID_ACQUISITION_DATE         | Simulates a scenario where acquisitionDate is later than disposalDate.                                   |   
| OUTSIDE_AMENDMENT_WINDOW         | Simulates the scenario where request cannot be completed as it is outside the amendment window.          | 
| STATEFUL                         | Performs a stateful create or update.                                                                    |
| REQUEST_CANNOT_BE_FULFILLED      | Simulates the scenario where the request cannot be fulfilled for various reasons other than the ones triggering other errors. |

**?source=latest** | Requesting **latest** source simulates success response with Latest disposals and overrides submitted. | | LOSS
**source=latest** | Requesting **latest** source with LOSS simulates success response with User provided disposals and overrides with losses. | | NOT_FOUND | Simulates the scenario where no data is found. | | STATEFUL | Performs a stateful retrieve.

put.description:
This endpoint enables you to override residential property disposal submissions previously submitted via HMRC
for payment for property disposal (PPD) (using the 'Report and pay Capital Gains Tax on UK property' service) for
a given National Insurance number and tax year.
**This endpoint can only be used after the tax year has ended.**

### Test data
Scenario simulation using Gov-Test-Scenario headers is only available in the sandbox environment.

| NOT_FOUND                        | Simulates the scenario where no disposals were found to override.                                           |
| PPD_SUBMISSION_ID_NOT_FOUND      | Simulates the scenario where a ppdSubmissionId used in the submission was not found.                        |

| OUTSIDE_AMENDMENT_WINDOW         | Simulates the scenario where request cannot be completed as it is outside the amendment window.             |

put.description:
This endpoint allows a developer to submit or amend the Winter Fuel Payment amount for a tax year.
A National Insurance number, tax year and the Winter Fuel Payment amount must be provided. The amount submitted must be either the minimum or maximum payment for that tax year, or zero if no payment was received.
This endpoint can only be used for tax years from 2026–27 onwards. 
**This endpoint can only be used after the tax year has ended.**

###  Test data
  Scenario simulation using Gov-Test-Scenario headers is only available in the sandbox environment.

  | Header Value (Gov-Test-Scenario) | Scenario                                                                                                                                                                                |
  |----------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
  | N/A - DEFAULT                    | Simulates success response.                                                                                                                                                             |
  | WFP_AMOUNT_ABOVE_MAXIMUM         | Simulates the scenario where the submitted amount exceeds the maximum Winter Fuel Payment for the tax year.                                                                             |
  | WFP_AMOUNT_BELOW_MINIMUM         | Simulates the scenario where the submitted amount is below the minimum Winter Fuel Payment for the tax year.                                                                            |
  | OUTSIDE_AMENDMENT_WINDOW         | Simulates the scenario where request cannot be completed as it is outside the amendment window.                                                                                         |
  | STATEFUL                         | Performs a stateful create or update. It uses fixed winter fuel payment amounts where 100 is the minimum and 300 is the maximum across all supported tax years for testing purposes.    |

The following groups of endpoints are stateful in the Sandbox: * [Dividends Income](#tag/Dividends-Income) * [UK Dividends Income](#tag/UK-Dividends-Income) * [Additional Directorship and Dividend Information](#tag/Additional-Directorship-and-Dividend-Information) # Send fraud prevention data HMRC monitors transactions to help protect your customers' confidential data from criminals and fraudsters.
! Warning You are required by law to submit header data for this API. This includes all associated APIs and endpoints.
[Check the data you need to send](/guides/fraud-prevention/). You can also use the [Test API](/api-documentation/docs/api/service/txm-fph-validator-api/2.0) during initial development and as part of your quality assurance checks. # Mapping APIs to Self Assessment tax return forms Some parameters in this API map to box numbers in one or more Self Assessment tax return forms. To learn more and to download this mapping information as a CSV file, go to [income-tax-mtd-changelog/mapping](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog?tab=readme-ov-file#mapping-apis-to-self-assessment-tax-return-forms) on GitHub. # Changelog You can find the changelog in the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/#readme) on GitHub. # Support * Direct reports of bugs or errors in Production or Sandbox code, or queries about HMRC business functionality (such as how a specific field is used by HMRC or why it is needed) to the [Software Development Support Team (SDST)](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/developer/support). * Send queries or feedback related to the design of the APIs (including recommended changes) using the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/issues) GitHub page. * Is this page not working properly? companyDirector.description: Indicates whether a taxable entity is a director or not.

closeCompany.description: Indicates whether the company is a close company. This field is always returned when companyDirector is true.

directorshipCeasedDate.description: Date when the directorship ceased. This will cease the rollover across tax years for custom employments that were created for Additional Dividends and Directorship. Must conform to the format `YYYY-MM-DD`

companyName.description: The name by which the company is registered with Companies House. This field is always returned when closeCompany is true.

companyNumber.description: The number by which the company is registered with Companies House. This field is always returned when closeCompany is true.

shareholding.description: The percentage shareholding of the company. This field is always returned when closeCompany is true. A value of 0 indicates no shareholding. The value must be between 0 and 100 up to 2 decimal places.

dividendReceived.description: The amount of dividends received from the company. This field is always returned when closeCompany is true. A value of 0 indicates no dividends were received. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

submittedOn.description: The date and time of the submission. Must conform to the format `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ`

companyDirector.description: Indicates whether a taxable entity is a director or not

companyName.description: The name by which the company is registered with Companies House. This is required where closeCompany is true.

companyNumber.description: The number by which the company is registered with Companies House. This is required where closeCompany is true.

shareholding.description:

dividendReceived.description:
The amount of dividends received from the company. This is required where closeCompany is true. Where no dividends are received, a zero can be submitted.

The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

! Warning You are required by law to submit header data for this API. This includes all associated APIs and endpoints.
[Check the data you need to send](/guides/fraud-prevention/). You can also use the [Test API](/api-documentation/docs/api/service/txm-fph-validator-api/1.0) during initial development and as part of your quality assurance checks. # Mapping APIs to Self Assessment tax return forms Some parameters in this API map to box numbers in one or more Self Assessment tax return forms. To learn more and to download this mapping information as a CSV file, go to [income-tax-mtd-changelog/mapping](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog?tab=readme-ov-file#mapping-apis-to-self-assessment-tax-return-forms) on GitHub. # Changelog You can find the changelog in the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/#readme) on GitHub. # Support * Direct reports of bugs or errors in Production or Sandbox code, or queries about HMRC business functionality (such as how a specific field is used by HMRC or why it is needed) to the [Software Development Support Team (SDST)](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/developer/support). * Send queries or feedback related to the design of the APIs (including recommended changes) using the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/issues) GitHub page. * Is this page not working properly? employment.description: Object containing the financial data relating to a single employment.

employmentSequenceNumber.description: A number that identifies the position of the employment in a sequence of employments for a given tax year.

payrollId.description: A unique identifier used by the employer to identify the employee. Must not be empty or contain only whitespace.

companyDirector.description: Identifies the employee as a director when set to True. This field will not be applicable for tax years 2025-26 onwards.

closeCompany.description: Identifies if the employer is a close company. This field will not be applicable for tax years 2025-26 onwards.

directorshipCeasedDate.description: The date the directorship ended. This field will not be applicable for tax years 2025-26 onwards. Must conform to the format YYYY-MM-DD

startDate.description: The date the employment began. Must conform to the format YYYY-MM-DD

cessationDate.description: The date the employment ended. Must conform to the format YYYY-MM-DD

occupationalPension.description: Indicates that the employee pays into an occupational pension when set to True.

disguisedRemuneration.description: Indicates that the employee is declaring disguised remuneration when set to True.

employer.description: Object containing pay details for a single employment.

employerRef.description: A unique identifier, the employer reference number.

employerName.description: The name of the employer the employee worked for.

pay.description: Object containing pay details for a single employment.

taxablePayToDate.description: The gross pay for this employment. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

totalTaxToDate.description: The amount of tax deducted for this employment. The value must be between -99999999999.99 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

paymentDate.description: The date of the latest payment. Must conform to the format YYYY-MM-DD

taxWeekNo.description: The week count of the tax year. The value must be an integer between 1 and 56

taxMonthNo.description: The month count of the tax year. The value must be an integer between 1 and 12

customerEstimatedPay.description: Object containing estimated pay details for a single employment.

amount.description: The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

deductions.description: Object containing details of deductions for a single employment.

studentLoans.description: Object containing details of deductions against student loans.

uglDeductionAmount.description: The amount deducted for an undergraduate student loan. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

pglDeductionAmount.description: The amount deducted for a postgraduate student loan. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

benefitsInKind.description: Object containing amount values of benefits received from a single employment.

accommodation.description: The value of accommodation costs provided by the employer. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

assets.description: The value of any goods provided by the employer not exclusively used for work. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

assetTransfer.description: The value of any company assets signed over by the employer. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

beneficialLoan.description: The amount of interest free or low interest loans given by the employer. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

car.description: The cash equivalent of any cars made available by the employer. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

carFuel.description: The amount paid for fuel when using company cars. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

educationalServices.description: Scholarships or school fees paid by the employer. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

entertaining.description: Entertainment costs paid by the employer either directly or reimbursed to the employee. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

expenses.description: Expenses reimbursed by the employer to the employee. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

medicalInsurance.description: The sum of insurance premiums paid by the employer for medical or dental insurance. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

telephone.description: Telephone costs paid by the employer that are not exempt. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

service.description: Services used by an employee and paid for by the employer. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

taxableExpenses.description: Taxable expenses reimbursed by the employer to the employee. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

van.description: The cash equivalent of any vans made available by the employer. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

vanFuel.description: The amount paid by the employer for fuel costs when using company vans. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

mileage.description: The mileage amount paid over HMRC's approved rate by the employer for use of employee's own car for work. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

nonQualifyingRelocationExpenses.description: Other costs involved in relocation paid for directly by the employer or reimbursed to the employee. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

nurseryPlaces.description: Childcare costs paid by the employer or voucher or commercial childcare costs above the exempt limit. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

otherItems.description: The value of any other benefits. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

paymentsOnEmployeesBehalf.description: Other costs incurred by the employee paid for by the employer. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

personalIncidentalExpenses.description: Incidental (non-business) expenses incurred by an employee while travelling on business. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

qualifyingRelocationExpenses.description: Employer paid costs associated with employee relocation including bridging loans. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

employerProvidedProfessionalSubscription.description: Professional fees and subscriptions paid for by the employer. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

employerProvidedServices.description: The value of services provided by the employer. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

incomeTaxPaidByDirector.description: Non PAYE Income Tax for directors deducted from the employer by HMRC. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

travelAndSubsistence.description: The cost of any travel and subsistence (accommodation, meals and so on) paid for by the employer, that is not exempt. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

vouchersAndCreditCards.description: The value of vouchers given by the employer and the expenditure of any employer provided credit cards. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

nonCash.description: The value of any other non-cash benefits paid to the employee. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

info.description:
The following groups of endpoints are stateful in the Sandbox: * [Employment Expenses](#tag/Employment-Expenses) * [Other Expenses](#tag/Other-Expenses) # Send fraud prevention data HMRC monitors transactions to help protect your customers' confidential data from criminals and fraudsters.
! Warning You are required by law to submit header data for this API. This includes all associated APIs and endpoints.
[Check the data you need to send](/guides/fraud-prevention/). You can also use the [Test API](/api-documentation/docs/api/service/txm-fph-validator-api/1.0) during initial development and as part of your quality assurance checks. # Mapping APIs to Self Assessment tax return forms Some parameters in this API map to box numbers in one or more Self Assessment tax return forms. To learn more and to download this mapping information as a CSV file, go to [income-tax-mtd-changelog/mapping](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog?tab=readme-ov-file#mapping-apis-to-self-assessment-tax-return-forms) on GitHub. # Changelog You can find the changelog in the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/#readme) on GitHub. # Support * Direct reports of bugs or errors in Production or Sandbox code, or queries about HMRC business functionality (such as how a specific field is used by HMRC or why it is needed) to the the [Software Development Support Team (SDST)](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/developer/support). * Send queries or feedback related to the design of the APIs (including recommended changes) using the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/issues) GitHub page. * Is this page not working properly? delete.description:
This endpoint allows a developer to delete employment expenses for a user and can only be used after the tax year has ended.
Deleting an expense will remove the amended expense and remove the "dateIgnored" flag from HMRC expenses. This endpoint requires a National Insurance number and tax year. ### Test data Scenario simulation using Gov-Test-Scenario headers is only available in the sandbox environment. | Header Value (Gov-Test-Scenario) | Scenario | |-----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | N/A - DEFAULT | Simulates success response. | | NOT_FOUND | Simulates the scenario where the given expenses could not be found. | | STATEFUL | Performs a stateful delete. | | OUTSIDE_AMENDMENT_WINDOW | Simulates the scenario where request cannot be completed as it is outside the amendment window. |

A National Insurance number and tax year must be provided. ### Test data Scenario simulation using Gov-Test-Scenario headers is only available in the sandbox environment. | Header Value (Gov-Test-Scenario) | Scenario | | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | N/A - DEFAULT

• submittedOn
• dateIgnored | | STATEFUL | Performs a stateful retrieve.

Information and data held by HMRC is not available in the sandbox environment. Providing ‘source=hmrcHeld’ will result in the expected HTTP 404 (matching resource not found) error being returned.

|

schema.description: Allows the retrieval of employment expenses

submittedOn.description:
The date the expenses were submitted.

Must conform to the format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSS'Z'

totalExpenses.description:
The sum of the expenses provided.

The value must be between  0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

source.description: Specifies the source of data returned.

dateIgnored.description:
The date the expenses were flagged not to be used in the tax calculation.

Must conform to the format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSS'Z'

expenses.description: Object containing the employment expenses.

businessTravelCosts.description:
Expenses associated with business travel where own or company vehicle was not used.

The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

jobExpenses.description:
The actual expense of replacing or maintaining tools or special work clothes.

The value must be between  0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

flatRateJobExpenses.description:
Fixed rate expenses applied for replacing or maintaining tools or special work clothes.

The value must be between  0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

professionalSubscriptions.description:
Fees or subscriptions to professional bodies, required in order to undertake the employment.

The value must be between  0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

hotelAndMealExpenses.description:
Subsistence costs incurred with work.

The value must be between  0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

otherAndCapitalAllowances.description:
The expense from purchasing small items required for this employment.

The value must be between  0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

vehicleExpenses.description:
Fuel and other costs when using a company vehicle.

The value must be between  0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

mileageAllowanceRelief.description:
The shortfall incurred when the employer pays less than the approved mileage rate.

The value must be between  0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

info.description:
The following endpoints are stateful in the Sandbox: * Retrieve Other Income * Create and Amend Other Income * Delete Other Income # Send fraud prevention data HMRC monitors transactions to help protect your customers' confidential data from criminals and fraudsters.
! Warning You are required by law to submit header data for this API. This includes all associated APIs and endpoints.
[Check the data you need to send](/guides/fraud-prevention/). You can also use the [Test API](/api-documentation/docs/api/service/txm-fph-validator-api/1.0) during initial development and as part of your quality assurance checks. # Mapping APIs to Self Assessment tax return forms Some parameters in this API map to box numbers in one or more Self Assessment tax return forms. To learn more and to download this mapping information as a CSV file, go to [income-tax-mtd-changelog/mapping](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog?tab=readme-ov-file#mapping-apis-to-self-assessment-tax-return-forms) on GitHub. # Changelog You can find the changelog in the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/#readme) on GitHub. # Support * Direct reports of bugs or errors in Production or Sandbox code, or queries about HMRC business functionality (such as how a specific field is used by HMRC or why it is needed) to the [Software Development Support Team (SDST)](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/developer/support). * Send queries or feedback related to the design of the APIs (including recommended changes) using the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/issues) GitHub page. * Is this page not working properly? This endpoint enables you to create and amend other income:
business receipts, overseas income and gains, chargeable foreign benefits and gifts, omitted foreign income, and all other income received whilst abroad.  
A National Insurance number and tax year must be provided.

Scenario simulation using Gov-Test-Scenario headers is only available in the sandbox environment.

| OUTSIDE_AMENDMENT_WINDOW         | Simulates the scenario where request cannot be completed as it is outside the amendment window.           |
| REQUEST_CANNOT_BE_FULFILLED      | Simulates the scenario where the request could not be processed.                                          |
| STATEFUL                         | Performs a stateful create or update.                                                                     |

info.description:
The following endpoints are stateful in the Sandbox: * Retrieve Other Income * Create and Amend Other Income * Delete Other Income # Send fraud prevention data HMRC monitors transactions to help protect your customers' confidential data from criminals and fraudsters.
! Warning You are required by law to submit header data for this API. This includes all associated APIs and endpoints.
[Check the data you need to send](/guides/fraud-prevention/). You can also use the [Test API](/api-documentation/docs/api/service/txm-fph-validator-api/1.0) during initial development and as part of your quality assurance checks. # Mapping APIs to Self Assessment tax return forms Some parameters in this API map to box numbers in one or more Self Assessment tax return forms. To learn more and to download this mapping information as a CSV file, go to [income-tax-mtd-changelog/mapping](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog?tab=readme-ov-file#mapping-apis-to-self-assessment-tax-return-forms) on GitHub. # Changelog You can find the changelog in the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/#readme) on GitHub. # Support * Direct reports of bugs or errors in Production or Sandbox code, or queries about HMRC business functionality (such as how a specific field is used by HMRC or why it is needed) to the [Software Development Support Team (SDST)](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/developer/support). * Send queries or feedback related to the design of the APIs (including recommended changes) using the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/issues) GitHub page. * Is this page not working properly? put.description:
This endpoint enables you to create and amend other income:
post-cessation receipts, business receipts, all other income received whilst abroad, overseas income and gains,
chargeable foreign benefits and gifts, omitted foreign income, benefits from pre-owned assets and additional taxable income.
A National Insurance number and tax year must be provided.

###  Test data
Scenario simulation using Gov-Test-Scenario headers is only available in the sandbox environment.


| Header Value (Gov-Test-Scenario) | Scenario                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| N/A - DEFAULT                    | Simulates success response.                                                                               |
| OUTSIDE_AMENDMENT_WINDOW         | Simulates the scenario where request cannot be completed as it is outside the amendment window.           |
| STATEFUL                         | Performs a stateful create or update.                                                                     |

parameters.description:

The minimum tax year is 2025-26. No gaps are allowed, for example, 2025-27 is not valid.

info.description:
The following endpoints are stateful in the Sandbox: * List All Partner Income Submissions * Create or Amend Partner Income * Retrieve Partner Income * Delete Partner Income # Send fraud prevention data HMRC monitors transactions to help protect your customers' confidential data from criminals and fraudsters.
! Warning You are required by law to submit header data for this API. This includes all associated APIs and endpoints.
[Check the data you need to send](/guides/fraud-prevention/). You can also use the [Test API](/api-documentation/docs/api/service/txm-fph-validator-api/1.0) during initial development and as part of your quality assurance checks. # Mapping APIs to Self Assessment tax return forms Some parameters in this API map to box numbers in one or more Self Assessment tax return forms. To learn more and to download this mapping information as a CSV file, go to [income-tax-mtd-changelog/mapping](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog?tab=readme-ov-file#mapping-apis-to-self-assessment-tax-return-forms) on GitHub. # Changelog You can find the changelog in the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/#readme) on GitHub. # Support * Direct reports of bugs or errors in Production or Sandbox code, or queries about HMRC business functionality (such as how a specific field is used by HMRC or why it is needed) to the [Software Development Support Team (SDST)](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/developer/support). * Send queries or feedback related to the design of the APIs (including recommended changes) using the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/issues) GitHub page. * Is this page not working properly? shareOfProfitOrLoss.description: The individual's share of the partnership's trading or professional profit or loss. The value must be between -99999999999.99 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

basisAdjustment.description: If your basis period is not the same as your accounting period, enter the adjustment needed to arrive at the profit or loss for the basis period. If the adjustment needs to be taken off the profit figure, this should be negative. The value must be between -99999999999.99 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

accountingAdjustment.description: The adjustment for change of accounting practice. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

foreignTaxClaimedDeduction.description: The foreign tax claimed as deduction only if Foreign Tax Credit Relief is not claimed. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

adjustedProfit.description: The individual's share of the partnership's profit of the year, after all statutory adjustments have been applied. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

transitionProfitArisingThisYear.description: The amount of transition profit treated as arising in the tax year. The value must be between 0 and 99999999999.99 up to 2 decimal places.

# Send fraud prevention data HMRC monitors transactions to help protect your customers' confidential data from criminals and fraudsters.
! Warning You are required by law to submit header data for this API. This includes all associated APIs and endpoints.
[Check the data you need to send](/guides/fraud-prevention/). You can also use the [Test API](/api-documentation/docs/api/service/txm-fph-validator-api/1.0) during initial development and as part of your quality assurance checks. # Mapping APIs to Self Assessment tax return forms Some parameters in this API map to box numbers in one or more Self Assessment tax return forms. To learn more and to download this mapping information as a CSV file, go to [income-tax-mtd-changelog/mapping](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog?tab=readme-ov-file#mapping-apis-to-self-assessment-tax-return-forms) on GitHub. # Changelog You can find the changelog in the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/#readme) on GitHub. # Support * Direct reports of bugs or errors in Production or Sandbox code, or queries about HMRC business functionality (such as how a specific field is used by HMRC or why it is needed) to the [Software Development Support Team (SDST)](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/developer/support). * Send queries or feedback related to the design of the APIs (including recommended changes) using the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/issues) GitHub page. * Is this page not working properly? ! Warning You are required by law to submit header data for this API. This includes all associated APIs and endpoints.
[Check the data you need to send](/guides/fraud-prevention/). You can also use the [Test API](/api-documentation/docs/api/service/txm-fph-validator-api/2.0) during initial development and as part of your quality assurance checks. # Mapping APIs to Self Assessment tax return forms Some parameters in this API map to box numbers in one or more Self Assessment tax return forms. To learn more and to download this mapping information as a CSV file, go to [income-tax-mtd-changelog/mapping](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog?tab=readme-ov-file#mapping-apis-to-self-assessment-tax-return-forms) on GitHub. # Changelog You can find the changelog in the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/#readme) on GitHub. # Support * Direct reports of bugs or errors in Production or Sandbox code, or queries about HMRC business functionality (such as how a specific field is used by HMRC or why it is needed) to the [Software Development Support Team (SDST)](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/developer/support). * Send queries or feedback related to the design of the APIs (including recommended changes) using the [income-tax-mtd-changelog](https://github.com/hmrc/income-tax-mtd-changelog/issues) GitHub page. * Is this page not working properly? bonusPaidYTD.description: The total bonus payment that has already been claimed and paid in the tax year to date. You can include an amount up to 2 decimal places.

reason.description: Confirm whether an additional bonus amount is due or funds need to be recovered.

eventDate.description: The date the return of information is sent. This cannot be in the future.

lisaManagerName.description: The name of the LISA provider.

taxYear.description: The tax year for the return of information. You cannot give the current tax year. You can only send a return of information for a previous tax year. Give the year that the tax year ends in. For example, for the 2017 to 2018 tax year give 2018.

marketValueCash.description: The total value of the cash LISA account. Give the value to the nearest whole pound. Do not include decimal places. For example, send 54.56 as 55. If you give a value for marketValueCash, give a value of 0 for marketValueStocksAndShares and annualSubsStocksAndShares.

marketValueStocksAndShares.description: The total value of the stocks and shares LISA account. Give the value to the nearest whole pound. Do not include decimal places. For example, send 54.56 as 55. If you give a value for marketValueStocksAndShares, give a value of 0 for marketValueCash and annualSubsCash.

annualSubsCash.description: The total value of subscriptions that the investor deposited into their cash LISA account during the tax year. Give the value to the nearest whole pound. Do not include decimal places. For example, send 54.56 as 55. If you give a value for annualSubsCash, give a value of 0 for marketValueStocksAndShares and annualSubsStocksAndShares.

annualSubsStocksAndShares.description: The total value of subscriptions that the investor deposited into their stocks and shares LISA account during the tax year. Give the value to the nearest whole pound. Do not include decimal places. For example, send 54.56 as 55. If you give a value for annualSubsStocksAndShares, give a value of 0 for marketValueCash and annualSubsCash.

originalLifeEventId.description: The lifeEventId of the original return of information affected by the correction. This is used together with the originalEventDate to make sure the right return of information is replaced.

originalEventDate.description: The eventDate of the original return of information affected by the correction.

items.title: Lifetime ISA Manager Accounts Events Life Event Id Response

lifeEventId.description: The ID for the life event.

eventDate.description: The date the life event occurred. This cannot be in the future.

lisaManagerName.description: The name of the LISA provider.

taxYear.description: The tax year for the return of information. This will be the year that the tax year ends in. For example, for the 2017 to 2018 tax year it will be 2018.

marketValueCash.description: The total value that was reported for the cash LISA account.

marketValueStocksAndShares.description: The total value that was reported for the stocks and shares LISA account.

annualSubsCash.description: The total value that was reported for investor subscriptions into their cash LISA account during the tax year.

annualSubsStocksAndShares.description: The total value that was reported for investor subscriptions into their stocks and shares LISA account during the tax year.

withdrawalAmount.description: This is the amount that the investor has withdrawn from the LISA account.

conveyancerReference.description: This is the reference for the conveyancer involved with the property purchase.

nameOrNumber.description: The name or number of the property that you requested funds to buy.

postalCode.description: The postcode of the property that you requested funds to buy.

allOf.description: The details of the property that you requested funds to buy.

fundReleaseId.description: The ID of the fund release for an extension or purchase outcome.

propertyPurchaseValue.description: The value of the property that the investor purchased. Only included if the purchase was completed.

allOf.description: Whether a property purchase was completed or failed.

originalLifeEventId.description: The ID of the life event that was corrected.

originalEventDate.description: The eventDate of the life event that was corrected.

allOf.description: Shows that a life event was corrected.

supersededBy.description: The ID of the life event that supersedes the current one.

lifeEventId.description: The reference number you get when you report a life event.

periodStartDate.description: The first date in the claim period. The periodStartDate must be the 6th day of the month. You cannot enter a date in the future for periodStartDate.

periodEndDate.description: The end date of the claim period. The periodEndDate must be the 5th day of the month. It has to be the month after the periodStartDate.

htbTransferInForPeriod.description: The total amount of Help to Buy funds in the account during the claim period. You can include an amount up to 2 decimal places.

htbTransferTotalYTD.description: The total amount of Help to Buy funds in the account in the tax year to date. You can include an amount up to 2 decimal places. If there is a number in htbTransferInForPeriod, then the number in htbTransferTotalYTD must be greater than 0.

allOf.description: Details about Help to Buy funds.

newSubsForPeriod.description: The total value of new qualifying deposits paid in to the account during the claim period. You can include an amount up to 2 decimal places.

newSubsYTD.description: The total value of new qualifying deposits paid in to the account during the tax year to date. You can include an amount up to 2 decimal places. If there is a number in newSubsForPeriod, then the number in newSubsYTD must be greater than 0.

totalSubsForPeriod.description: The total amount in the account during the claim period that qualifies for a bonus payment. You can include an amount up to 2 decimal places. The totalSubsForPeriod must always be greater than 0 except when bonusDueForPeriod is 0.

totalSubsYTD.description: The total amount in the account during the tax year to date that qualifies for a bonus payment. You can include an amount up to 2 decimal places. The totalSubsYTD must be the same as or more than totalSubsForPeriod.

allOf.description: Details about qualifying deposits and account balance.

bonusDueForPeriod.description: The total bonus payment amount due for the claim period. You can include an amount up to 2 decimal places. If you supersede this claim and the supersededReason is ‘bonus recovery’, then the bonusDueForPeriod can be 0. If not, it must always be greater than 0.

totalBonusDueYTD.description: The total bonus payment amount due for the tax year to date. You can include an amount up to 2 decimal places. This cannot be less than bonusDueForPeriod.

bonusPaidYTD.description: The total bonus payment that has already been claimed and paid in the tax year to date. You can include an amount up to 2 decimal places.

claimReason.description: The reason the bonus payment was claimed.

allOf.description: Bonus payment details.

automaticRecoveryAmount.description: This is the amount HMRC can collect from the LISA manager in bonus recovery cases. If there are no funds available, this value must be 0.

originalTransactionId.description: The transactionId of the original bonus affected by the correction or recovery. This is used together with the originalBonusDueForPeriod to make sure the right bonus transaction is replaced.

originalBonusDueForPeriod.description: This is how much was in the bonusDueForPeriod in the original bonus request.

transactionResult.description: The amount to be added to or recovered from the original bonus.

reason.description: Confirm whether an additional bonus amount is due or funds need to be recovered.

allOf.description: Correct an existing bonus claim with an additional bonus or a recovery of an overpaid amount.

info.description:
# Authorisation

The endpoints in this API are [user-restricted](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/api-documentation/docs/authorisation/user-restricted-endpoints).
Your users must grant authority for your software to access them by signing in to their HMRC online account.

The API supports individual and agent users. Note that:
- Individual users can only access their own information.
- Agent users can only access their own clients’ data.

The following options are supported for agents:
  
**Option 1: Agent services account**

If the agent uses an [agent services account](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/hmrc-online-services-for-agents#agent-services-account), they can access their [existing 64-8 clients](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/how-to-get-authorised-to-act-as-a-tax-agent-on-behalf-of-your-clients#get-authorised-using-online-services-online-forms-or-paper-forms) who they have linked to their agent services account (restricted to 2 years’ history).

**Option 2: HMRC online services for agents account**
  
If the agent uses an [HMRC online services for agents account](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/hmrc-online-services-for-agents#hmrc-online-services-for-agents-account) which is enrolled for [Self Assessment for Agents](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/self-assessment-for-agents-online-service), they will be able to access their [existing 64-8 clients](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/how-to-get-authorised-to-act-as-a-tax-agent-on-behalf-of-your-clients#get-authorised-using-online-services-online-forms-or-paper-forms) (restricted to 2 years’ history).

info.description:
# Overview
Use this API to get HMRC Assist feedback about potential inaccuracies in returns before they are formally submitted.

The endpoints must be used in this order:
1. Use the *feedback* endpoint to send draft return data, and receive HMRC Assist feedback messages about that data.
2. Use the *acknowledge* endpoint to confirm that your software has presented the HMRC Assist feedback messages to the user. If there is no feedback (a single message with *itemNumber* "0"), the response has no *correlationId* and you do not need to acknowledge it.

Because this process operates on draft, unfinalised data, requesting feedback carries no formal declaration. Also, the process does not block formal declaration submission via the *returns* endpoint of the [VAT (MTD) API](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/api-documentation/docs/api/service/vat-api/). Your software must allow customers to submit their VAT return, irrespective of any HMRC Assist submission feedback.

For more information about HMRC Assist for VAT, see the [VAT (MTD) end-to-end service guide](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/guides/vat-mtd-end-to-end-service-guide/documentation/hmrc-assist-for-vat.html).

The response will contain feedback messages in English and Welsh, highlighting potential mistakes or discrepancies in the VAT return data. **Note:** Before using this endpoint, you must first call the obligations endpoint on the [VAT (MTD) API](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/api-documentation/docs/api/service/vat-api/) to get the period key. ### Test data

Scenario simulations using Gov-Test-Scenario headers are only available in the sandbox environment.

Header Value (Gov-Test-Scenario) Scenario

Default (No header value)

Simulates the scenario where there is one HMRC Assist feedback message.

MULTIPLE_FEEDBACK

Simulates the scenario where there is more than one HMRC Assist feedback message.

NO_FEEDBACK

Simulates the scenario where there is no HMRC Assist feedback.

INVALID_VRN

Simulates the scenario where the VRN has not passed validation.

INVALID_PERIODKEY

Simulates the scenario where the periodKey has not passed validation.

INVALID_REQUEST

Simulates the scenario where the request body has not passed validation.

TAX_PERIOD_NOT_ENDED

Simulates the scenario where the accounting period has not ended.

INSOLVENT_TRADER

Simulates the scenario where the client is an insolvent trader.

periodKey.description: The ID code for the period that this obligation belongs to. This should be obtained from the obligations endpoint of the [VAT (MTD) API](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/api-documentation/docs/api/service/vat-api/). The format is a string of four alphanumeric characters. Occasionally the format includes the # symbol.

vatDueSales.description: VAT due on sales and other outputs. This corresponds to box 1 on the VAT Return form.

vatDueAcquisitions.description: VAT due in the period on acquisitions of goods made in Northern Ireland from EU Member States. This corresponds to box 2 on the VAT Return form.

totalVatDue.description: Total VAT due (the sum of vatDueSales and vatDueAcquisitions). This corresponds to box 3 on the VAT Return form.

vatReclaimedCurrPeriod.description: VAT reclaimed in the period on purchases and other inputs (including acquisitions in Northern Ireland from EU member states). This corresponds to box 4 on the VAT Return form.

netVatDue.description:
The absolute difference between the *totalVatDue* and
*vatReclaimedCurrPeriod* values. This should therefore be a positive
number, calculated by subtracting the smallest value from the
largest. HMRC will automatically determine whether the number
represents net VAT that is due or net VAT that can be reclaimed.

This corresponds to box 5 on the VAT Return form.

totalValueSalesExVAT.description: Total value of sales and all other outputs excluding any VAT. This corresponds to box 6 on the VAT Return form. The value must be in whole pounds (no pence).

totalValuePurchasesExVAT.description: Total value of purchases and all other inputs excluding any VAT (including exempt purchases). This corresponds to box 7 on the VAT Return form. The value must be in whole pounds (no pence).

totalValueGoodsSuppliedExVAT.description: Total value of dispatches of goods and related costs (excluding VAT) from Northern Ireland to EU Member States. This corresponds to box 8 on the VAT Return form. The value must be in whole pounds (no pence).

totalAcquisitionsExVAT.description: Total value of acquisitions of goods and related costs (excluding VAT) made in Northern Ireland from EU Member States. This corresponds to box 9 on the VAT Return form. The value must be in whole pounds (no pence).

info.description:
# Data availability

Data is available for taxpayers who, in the given tax year, have:

- self-employment income
- self-employment and employment income

Class 1 NICable earnings data is not available until Class 1 NICs reconciliation is complete. This starts in May and is usually complete by the end of August. Before reconciliation, Class 1 NICable earnings is returned as £0.00.

Class 2 NI contributions data should be available immediately at the end of the relevant tax year. However it can change after that date due to Class 1 NICs reconciliation or if we receive late changes from the taxpayer.

Find out more about [National Insurance](https://www.gov.uk/national-insurance/overview).

# Authorisation

The endpoint in this API is [user-restricted](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/api-documentation/docs/authorisation/user-restricted-endpoints).
Your users must grant authority for your software to access it by signing in to their HMRC online account.

The API supports individual and agent users. Note that:
- Individual users can only access their own information.
- Agent users can only access their own clients’ data.

The following options are supported for agents:

**Option 1: Agent services account**

If the agent uses an [agent services account](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/hmrc-online-services-for-agents#agent-services-account), they can access their [existing 64-8 clients](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/how-to-get-authorised-to-act-as-a-tax-agent-on-behalf-of-your-clients#get-authorised-using-online-services-online-forms-or-paper-forms) who they have linked to their agent services account (restricted to 2 years’ history).

**Option 2: HMRC online services for agents account**

If the agent uses an [HMRC online services for agents account](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/hmrc-online-services-for-agents#hmrc-online-services-for-agents-account) which is enrolled for [Self Assessment for Agents](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/self-assessment-for-agents-online-service), they will be able to access their [existing 64-8 clients](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/how-to-get-authorised-to-act-as-a-tax-agent-on-behalf-of-your-clients#get-authorised-using-online-services-online-forms-or-paper-forms) (restricted to 2 years’ history).

This endpoint allows a developer to retrieve the final declaration (previously known as crystallisation) obligations for a customer’s Income Tax account. The account identifier (National Insurance number) must be provided. ### Test data Scenario simulation using Gov-Test-Scenario headers is only available in the sandbox environment. | Header Value (Gov-Test-Scenario) | Scenario | |---------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | N/A - DEFAULT | Simulates a success response with an open obligation. | | MULTIPLE | Simulates a success response with multiple obligations. | | INSOLVENT_TRADER | Simulates a scenario where the remote endpoint indicates that the trader is insolvent. | | NOT_FOUND | Simulates a scenario where no data is found. | | DYNAMIC | The following response values will change to correspond to the values submitted in the request:
• periodStartDate
• periodEndDate
• dueDate
• receivedDate|

The earliest allowable tax year is 2017-18.

For a response with a self-employment business, use businessId:
• XBIS12345678903
For a response with a UK property business, use businessId:
• XPIS12345678903
For a response with a foreign property business, use businessId:
• XFIS12345678903 | | FULFILLED | Simulates a success response with a fulfilled obligation.

For a response with a self-employment business, use businessId:
• XBIS12345678902
For a response with a UK property business, use businessId:
